newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China EB-IHD raises HK$1.9 bln for bank.
newsitem.headline: China EB-IHD raises HK$1.9 bln for bank.

text.p: China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd said it had agreed to buy a 20 percent stake in Everbright Bank of China for about HK$2.4 billion and would raise HK$1.9 billion in a new share issue to help fund the purchase.

The company said in a statement on Wednesday that it had agreed to buy the 20 percent stake from its parent China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd and would issue 168.89 million new shares to its controlling shareholder at HK$11.25 per share.
China Everbright-IHD said it would use HK$500 million in cash received from a HK$1.9 billion share issue earlier this month to pay for the balance.
The previous share issue involved 175.55 million new shares subscribed by China Everbright Holdings at HK$10.75 per share.
China Everbright-IHD said the remaining proceeds of that issue would be used to fund future acquisitions and repay about HK$380 million in shareholders' loans.

It said the decision to issue more new shares for the bank purchase instead of using the proceeds from the previous share issue reflected China Everbright Holdings' desire to increase its stake. After the transactions, the parent will indirectly hold about 56.9 percent of China Everbright-IHD's share capital compared with a current 40.02 percent.

The estimated net profit for the bank in 1997 was guaranteed by the seller to be no less than 1.07 billion yuan (HK$999.9 million) according to Chinese accounting standards (PRC GAAP) and 914.5 million yuan (HK$851.0 million) according to international accounting standards (IAS), the statement said.
The price/earnings multiple implied by the total consideration being paid is 14.1 times based on IAS guaranteed profit, it said.
The price to book value ratio based on 1996 IAS shareholders' equity is 2.97 times, it said.
Everbright Bank was established in Beijing in August 1992 by the China Everbright Group Ltd, which is directly under the control of China's State Council.
Folllowing a restructuring and capital expansion which was completed on January 15, 1997, the bank became a joint stock commercial bank.

The bank is one of six national commercial banks in China with a network of 13 branches, including its headquarters. The bank is principally engaged in renminbi and foreign currency deposit-taking, individual savings deposit-taking, commercial lending, inter-bank borrowing and lending, money market operations and other activities.
